$comment: Declarative expectations for ops/execution_watchdog.py.
Workflow A schedules are NOT listed here: the watchdog derives them from
workflow_a_control.client_dataset_schedule so enabling or disabling a dataset
automatically changes what is expected. Only schedules that have no database
metadata of their own belong in this file.
Backup and prune are deliberately absent: they persist no public.runs row, so
there is nothing here for the watchdog to assert against. Their failures are
covered by systemd OnFailure= routing into ops/systemd_failure_adapter.py.
Grace windows are execution-time budgets, not guesses. Workflow B orchestrator
runs have taken up to ~109 minutes in production, so 180 minutes leaves real
headroom before a missing-run incident is raised.
suspected-bug-email-worker.timer fires every 5 minutes and the worker
stamps a heartbeat on every completed batch, including empty ones. A
30-minute grace is six consecutive missed fires — long enough that host
load or a single slow SMTP batch cannot trip it, short enough that a
stopped alert channel is found within one scan.
This subject is why a dead alert worker is observable at all: it delivers
nothing when idle, so public.runs cannot distinguish 'nothing to send'
from 'not running'. Reported by the watchdog, a different unit and a
different process, so the worker is never asked to report itself.
heartbeats.subject: alerting_email_worker
heartbeats.consequence: No queued operator alert can be delivered while it is down.

$alert_delivery_comment: Durable half of the dead-letter contract. The worker's non-zero exit makes a
dead-letter transition visible as a failed unit, but only momentarily: the
row is never re-claimed, so the next batch succeeds and clears the unit
state while the alert is still undelivered. This subject keeps asserting
'there are alerts nobody will ever receive' until an operator clears them.
180 minutes is not a guess: the worker retries with bounded exponential
backoff up to SUSPECTED_BUG_EMAIL_MAX_RETRY_SECONDS (default 3600), so a
healthy row can legitimately sit queued for roughly an hour between
attempts. Anything below ~2h would alert on working backoff.
